findings.description: The bucket is explicitly noted and configured to be public, allowing unauthenticated or unintended access to stored objects including the customer-master.xlsx file, resulting in potential data exposure.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for the bucket, meaning data at rest is stored unencrypted and vulnerable to exposure if underlying storage is compromised.
A sensitive file (customer-master.xlsx, likely containing customer PII) is uploaded to the aws_s3_bucket.data bucket, which is public and unencrypted, directly exposing sensitive customer data.
The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so financial data stored in this bucket is not encrypted at rest, increasing risk of data exposure.
The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects are stored unencrypted at rest, risking data exposure if underlying storage or backups are compromised.
No logging block is configured for this bucket, so there is no audit trail of access requests, hindering detection of unauthorized access.
The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects stored in it (potentially sensitive data science data) are unencrypted at rest.
